## Summary  
The 2025 cotton crop in Limestone County is finished. The county‑level yield estimate is **1082 lb/acre** with an 80 % range of 871 to 1284 lb/acre. The season showed mixed weather effects on the estimate.

## Crop health  
Peak NDVI was 0.76 on 2025‑08‑14. Peak NDRE was 0.55. Clear satellite images were available on 32 dates. The field showed a low NDVI zone in the north.

## Problem areas  
A low‑NDVI zone covers 33.4 % of the field, 92.3 acres, in the north. Soil pH values of 5.3 and 5.0 are below the optimal 6.0 to 6.5 range. Some Ooltewah silt loam is somewhat poorly drained. The water balance shows a moderate deficit.

## Weather  
Total rain was 28.6 in. Water balance was –2.1 in. Heat stress days were 0. The longest dry spell was 15 days. Deficit severity is moderate.

## Soil  
Field available water is 6.5 in. The dominant soils are Cumberland silty clay loam with pH 5.3 and well‑drained conditions. A portion of the field has Ooltewah silt loam with pH 5.0 and somewhat poorly drained status.

## Yield outlook  
Summer heat averaged 88.9 F versus a typical 90.8 F, which raised the estimate. August water balance was –3.6 in versus a typical –1.7 in, which lowered the estimate. Longest dry spell was 17.0 days versus a typical 22.8 days, which lowered the estimate. Summer rainfall was 12.4 in versus a typical 14.6 in, which raised the estimate.

## What to check next  
- Apply lime to raise soil pH toward 6.0‑6.5.  
- Improve drainage in areas with somewhat poorly drained soils.  
- Monitor residual moisture in the low‑NDVI north zone.  
- Review planting dates and soil temperature for the next season.
